title: Dixieland forgotten in the late Twenties; forming a band with Gus and Victor Spencer
summary: Joe says he did not miss Dixieland while playing tunes of the day, and after the ship he, Gus and Victor Spencer started their own band in Los Angeles.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: All this time, really, that you'd...like from the medicine almost clean through, you'd more or less sort of laid down playing Dixieland music, hadn't you?

Oh, yes. That period you forgot about Dixieland. You played the tunes of the day. They had no Dixieland band in Seattle at that time at all. We had forgot about... Earl Thompson had just come out of a big band, the Speed Webb band.
Did it matter to you, or did you...?

I didn't miss it. I really didn't miss it. Because like I said, we didn't play that much Dixieland to start with. When you played in a taxi dance... And Gus and I, when we came back down from that trip, Gus, Victor Spencer and I got together a bunch of guys, about eight or nine pieces, and started a band of our own. And that's where we would play, on 15th and Main in Los Angeles, they had a big dance hall...
